title: Stale reservation reaping in doctor
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: reservations whose owner died linger until they cause a BOREAL_CONFLICT claim (1 in the audit) or coordinator babysitting. Heartbeat and lock machinery already exist (heartbeat create/advance/show, lock inspect/break). Change: doctor detects reservations past their expiry or with lapsed heartbeats and, under --strict or an explicit --repair flag, releases them with a ledger-recorded reaped reason; prime surfaces the count (prime --json already reports expiredActiveCount, so the detection signal partially exists — this task adds the visible finding plus the safe repair path). Where: doctor implementation, reservation lifecycle in packages/engine/src/runtime.ts. Constraint: reaping is opt-in via the repair flag, never silent; the reaped event must name the original owner and expiry so finish-after-reap produces a clear terminal error for the dead agent.
acceptanceCriteria: doctor reports expired/heartbeat-lapsed reservations as findings
Repair flag releases them with a ledger-recorded reaped reason naming owner and expiry
A reaped agent calling finish gets a terminal error explaining the reap, not a bare NOT_FOUND
